# Canonical required-tool list for adopter-chosen container images
# (specs/038-runner-container-passthrough research.md D6, contracts/
# runner-container-passthrough.md "Image prerequisite contract").
#
# Read by three consumers that must stay in agreement structurally, not by
# convention (FR-011a):
#   - every stage file's verify-image-prerequisites job (T003) embeds this
#     same list literally as REQUIRED_TOOLS in its tool-check step;
#   - lint-workflows.yml's Gate 23 (T032) compares each stage's embedded
#     list against this file and fails on drift;
#   - lint-workflows.yml's Gate 62 (specs/054-e2e-container-coverage)
#     builds wing-commander's own e2e reference image
#     (.github/docker/e2e-reference-image/Dockerfile) and inspects it
#     against this file directly, the one consumer that can fail if the
#     Dockerfile itself stops installing a tool the text still claims to.
#
# One tool name per line. '#'-prefixed and blank lines are ignored.
#
# node is an INFERRED dependency, not one this repository's own run:
# blocks directly invoke: anthropics/claude-code-action@v1 (used by every
# agent-bearing job across all eleven stages) is a JavaScript action, which
# implies a Node.js runtime requirement this repository's own source cannot
# confirm or deny (research.md D6). Included on that inference, not on
# direct evidence — a decision recorded here rather than silently assumed.
# timeout is a DIRECT dependency, added by specs/039-lifecycle-gate-retry:
# wing-commander-lifecycle-gate wraps its `gh issue view` read in
# `timeout "$read_timeout" ...` so a hung read becomes a retryable 124
# rather than a stalled stage. That action runs INSIDE the adopter's
# container (every gated stage's job carries container: image:), so the
# image has to provide it. It was previously assumed present under Gate
# 23's ALWAYS_AVAILABLE coreutils set, which is exactly how a hard
# dependency reached eleven stages without ever being declared here.
# unzip is an INDIRECT dependency: anthropics/claude-code-action@v1's first
# step, "Install Bun" (oven-sh/setup-bun), downloads bun-linux-x64.zip and
# extracts it with unzip, so every agent-bearing job dies before Claude
# Code starts on an image without it. Intake run 37866026318 (job
# 113612908101) on wing-commander's own e2e reference image failed there
# with "Unable to locate executable file: unzip." while this check, which
# did not yet list unzip, had passed the image. It was previously assumed
# present under Gate 23's ALWAYS_AVAILABLE set, as timeout was.
#
# This list is an INFERENCE, cross-checked rather than proven by the agent
# start-up check (specs/112-agent-startup-image-check): the daily
# private-image dogfood run (startup-check input) runs the real agent action's
# setup in the image and names the step that fails. The git floor (>= 2.38,
# image-git-floor.sh) is checked in the same probe as presence; the 2.38
# minimum is the oldest git the agent action's checkout handling is
# known to work with, and unzip is listed on the evidence above.
#
# Presence is all this contract checks, for `timeout` as for `gh`. A
# BusyBox build older than 1.30 (2018) provides the applet but requires
# `-t DURATION`, so it would pass the check and still fail the call. Not
# guarded against: an image that old cannot run this pipeline for other
# reasons, and a usability probe would have to be written per tool.
git
gh
jq
curl
python3
bash
node
timeout
unzip
